questions.question: Find the remainder when the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 12, 15 and 25 is divided by 9.
questions.solution:
**Given values:** A number divisible by 12, 15, and 25

**Concept: **

The number is the least common multiple (LCM) of 12, 15, and 25. The remainder when a number is divided by 9 is the same as the remainder when the sum of its digits is divided by 9.

**Calculation:**

⇒ The LCM of 12, 15, and 25 is 300. The smallest 6-digit number divisible by 300 is 100200.

⇒ Sum of digits of 100200 = 1 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 0 = 3

⇒ Remainder when 3 is divided by 9 = 3

**Therefore, the remainder when the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 12, 15, and 25 is divided by 9 is 3.

300 × 334 = 100200

So, the smallest 6-digit number which is divisible by 12, 15 and 25 is = 100200

When 100200 is divided by 9 then the remainder is:

100200 = 9 × 11133 + 3

questions.question: The total salary of A and B is Rs. 1215. A spent 855over7% of his income and B spent 831over3% of his income. The ratio of saving is 3 : 4. Find their individual salary.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A's savings % = 100% − 85(5/7)% = 100% − 600/7% = 100/7% = 1/7 of A's salary.

B's savings % = 100% − 83(1/3)% = 100% − 250/3% = 50/3% = 1/6 of B's salary.

Ratio of savings ⇒ A/7 : B/6 = 3 : 4 ⇒ 6A / 7B = 3 / 4 ⇒ A : B = 7 : 8

Total salary = 7 + 8 = 15 units = 1215 ⇒ 1 unit = 81

A's salary = 7 × 81 = 567 and B's salary = 8 × 81 = 648.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 567, Rs. 648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total salary of A and B = Rs. 1215

A's expenditure = 85(5/7)% and B's expenditure = 83(1/3)%

Ratio of their savings = 3 : 4

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income × (100% − Expenditure%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d43eef8dda0f7d4b703b674de8593233eeb8751273ac0a2350198bd4a7a70c2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A's savings = 100% − 85(5/7)% = (100 − 600/7)% = 100/7% = 1/7

⇒ B's savings = 100% − 83(1/3)% = (100 − 250/3)% = 50/3% = 1/6

⇒ Ratio of savings = (1/7 × A) / (1/6 × B) = 3 / 4

⇒ (6 × A) / (7 × B) = 3 / 4

⇒ A / B = (3 × 7) / (4 × 6) = 21 / 24 = 7 / 8

⇒ Total salary ratio = 7 + 8 = 15 parts

⇒ 15 parts = Rs. 1215

⇒ 1 part = 1215 ÷ 15 = Rs. 81

⇒ A's salary = 7 × 81 = Rs. 567

⇒ B's salary = 8 × 81 = Rs. 648

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 567, Rs. 648.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting complex percentages into fractions saves calculation time. For instance, 14(2/7)% = 1/7 and 16(2/3)% = 1/6. By extending this, 85(5/7)% directly converts to 6/7, and 83(1/3)% translates to 5/6.

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

Always apply the basic equation: Income = Expenditure + Savings. If values are presented in percentages, you can subtract from 100% to directly fetch the missing entity.

Ratio Distribution

When any total quantity is distributed among entities in the ratio m : n, their respective shares are given by (m / (m + n)) × Total and (n / (m + n)) × Total.
</p

questions.question: What is revenue deficit?

options.text: It is the excess of government's total expenditure over total receipts.
It is the difference between revenue and capital expenditure.
It is the excess of government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
It is the excess of government's capital expenditure over capital receipts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is, '**It is excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts**'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue** means **income or earnings,** and **deficit** means **shortage.**
 
• A revenue deficit is a condition when expenditure is more than earnings.
 
 
• In some business terms, it means the difference between projected (assumed) income and realized (actual earned) income.
 
 
 
• So,** a revenue deficit is the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Excess of the government's total expenditure over total receipts** is called a** fiscal deficit.**
 
• **Capital expenditures** are one-time **long-term expenses**.
 
 
• Examples - ***Machinery, Vehicles, Land, etc.***
 
 
 
• **Revenue expenditures** are short-term and **day-to-day expenses**.
 
 
• Examples - ***Rent, Bills, etc.***
 
 
 
• **Excess of the government's capital expenditure over capital receipts** is a **capital deficit.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper sells goods to a customer at a profit of T% over the cost price and also weighs 800 g instead of 1 kg. His total profit percentage is 40%. What is the value of T?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total profit multiplier = Markup multiplier × Weight error multiplier.

Given total profit is 40%, multiplier = 140/100 = 1.4.

Weight error multiplier = True Weight ÷ Faulty Weight = 1000 ÷ 800 = 1.25.

Markup multiplier (1 + T/100) = Total profit multiplier ÷ Weight error multiplier = 1.4 ÷ 1.25 = 1.12.

1 + T/100 = 1.12 ⇒ T/100 = 0.12 ⇒ T = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP per kg = Rs. 1000 (assumed), Customer pays for 1 kg but receives 800 g. Total Profit% = 40%.

**Formulas:** Total Profit% = [ (True Value − Error) × (100 + T) / (Error × 100) − 1 ] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a4ae870bc9d74cde0b4f96b00725ce552c4535b5c663ca74e5b9d9c20a5d3a77.png] 

⇒ Let CP of 1 g = Rs. 1. So, CP of 1000 g = Rs. 1000 and CP of 800 g = Rs. 800.

⇒ The shopkeeper sells 800 g but charges for 1000 g at a profit of T%.

⇒ SP = 1000 × (100 + T) / 100 = 10 × (100 + T).

⇒ Total Profit% = [(SP − CP of 800g) / CP of 800g] × 100 = 40.

⇒ [10(100 + T) − 800] / 800 = 40 / 100 = 0.4.

⇒ 1000 + 10T − 800 = 320 ⇒ 200 + 10T = 320.

⇒ 10T = 120 ⇒ T = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses less weight, the **Effective Gain%** is calculated on the actual weight delivered to the customer. Formula: Gain% = [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100.

Combined Profit

If there is both a price markup and a weight shortage, the **Overall Profit** is the result of successive multiplication of individual profit factors.</p

questions.question: The traffic lights at 3 different road crossings change after every 48 sec, 72 sec and 108 sec respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 8:20 am, then what time they will again change simultaneously ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The lights will change simultaneously after an interval equal to the LCM of their individual times.

LCM of 48, 72, and 108 = 432 seconds.

Converting to minutes: 432 seconds = 7 minutes and 12 seconds.

Next simultaneous change = 8:20:00 am + 7 min 12 sec = 8:27:12 am.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:27:12 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Traffic light 1 interval = 48 sec

Traffic light 2 interval = 72 sec

Traffic light 3 interval = 108 sec

Time of first simultaneous change = 8:20:00 am

**Formula Used:**

Next simultaneous change = Initial time + LCM(t₁, t₂, t₃)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 48 = 2⁴ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 108 = 2² × 3³

⇒ LCM(48, 72, 108) = 2⁴ × 3³

⇒ LCM = 16 × 27 = 432 seconds

⇒ Convert 432 seconds into minutes = 432 ÷ 60

⇒ 432 seconds = 7 minutes and 12 seconds

⇒ Adding this interval to the initial given time:

⇒ Next change time = 8:20:00 am + 00:07:12

⇒ Next change time = 8:27:12 am

**∴ The correct answer is 8:27:12 am.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest multiple that is exactly divisible by every member of a set of numbers. It is primarily used to determine when multiple periodic events will synchronize and happen together again.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides all the given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is commonly used for dividing different quantities into the largest possible equal groups.

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For any two specific numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their LCM and HCF: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b).

Fractions Rule for LCM

To calculate the exact LCM of multiple fractions, use the direct formula: LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).
</p

questions.question: 12 women and 16 men can do a piece of work in 5 days. 13 women and 24 men can do it in 4 days. How long will 25 women and 50 men take to do it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate total work: 5 × (12W + 16M) = 4 × (13W + 24M)

⇒ 60W + 80M = 52W + 96M ⇒ 8W = 16M ⇒ 1W = 2M

Convert Group 1 to men only: 12(2M) + 16M = 40M, taking 5 days.

Target group in men only: 25(2M) + 50M = 100M.

Using M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ ⇒ 40 × 5 = 100 × D ⇒ D = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Group 1: 12 Women (W) and 16 Men (M) can do the work in 5 days.

Group 2: 13 Women (W) and 24 Men (M) can do the work in 4 days.

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to determine the efficiency of each group and then solve for the individual efficiencies of men and women.

 
 

 **Persons**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 12W + 16M
 5
 20
 20 ÷ 5 = 4
 
 

 13W + 24M
 4
 20 ÷ 4 = 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 12W + 16M = 4 (Equation 1)

⇒ 13W + 24M = 5 (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 3 and Equation 2 by 2 to balance M:

⇒ 36W + 48M = 12

⇒ 26W + 48M = 10

⇒ Subtracting the two equations: 10W = 2 ⇒ W = 0.2 units/day

⇒ Substituting W = 0.2 into Equation 1: 12(0.2) + 16M = 4

⇒ 2.4 + 16M = 4 ⇒ 16M = 1.6 ⇒ M = 0.1 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of target group (25W + 50M) = 25(0.2) + 50(0.1) = 5 + 5 = 10 units/day

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total work is the product of efficiency and the time taken to complete it. For equivalent groups completing the same task, the work relation is W = M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂.

Combined Efficiency

When individuals with different capabilities work together, their one-day work (efficiency) is added directly. The combined efficiency of a mixed group is (Number of men × Men's efficiency) + (Number of women × Women's efficiency).

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

The efficiency concept is closely mirrored in Pipes & Cisterns problems, where the work done corresponds to the volume filled, and efficiency equates to the filling rate of different pipes.
</p

questions.question: If p + q = 7 and p² + q² = 25, then find the value of pq.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For small values, use **hit and trial** by identifying factors or pairs of numbers.

Given **p + q = 7** and **p² + q² = 25**, check pairs that sum to 7:

(3, 4) ⇒ 3 + 4 = 7 and 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25. This satisfies both conditions.

The product **pq** = 3 × 4 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given values: **p + q = 7** and **p² + q² = 25**

Formula used: **(p + q)² = p² + q² + 2pq**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02303362b228b95c1285cf5dae74109473803459c4f666776abca6fc69263769.png] 

Applying the **algebraic identity**:

⇒ (p + q)² = 7²

⇒ p² + q² + 2pq = 49

⇒ 25 + 2pq = 49

⇒ 2pq = 49 − 25

⇒ 2pq = 24

⇒ pq = 24 ÷ 2

⇒ pq = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square of a Difference

(p − q)² = p² + q² − 2pq. This formula is used when the difference and sum of squares are known.

Difference of Squares

p² − q² = (p − q)(p + q). This identity helps in factorizing quadratic expressions.

Relationship between Identities

(p + q)² − (p − q)² = 4pq. This is useful for finding the product directly from the sum and difference.</p

questions.question: There are 24 lambs, 36 goats and 60 sheep and they have to be arranged in several rows so that every row contains the same number of animals of only one type. What is the minimum number of rows required for this to happen?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To minimize the **number of rows**, maximize the **number of animals** in each row.

HCF of 24, 36, and 60 = 12 (Animals per row).

Total rows = (24 ÷ 12) + (36 ÷ 12) + (60 ÷ 12) = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 rows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Lambs = 24, Goats = 36, Sheep = 60.

**Formula Used:** Minimum Rows = (Total Sum of Items) ÷ (HCF of Items).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddc1d2dd544154c02db0651052b637025b95de21ce7092baf75a161dbf16d4be.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Find the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of 24, 36, and 60.

⇒ Factors of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

⇒ Factors of 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

⇒ Factors of 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ **HCF** = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 (Maximum animals per row).

⇒ Rows for Lambs = 24 ÷ 12 = 2

⇒ Rows for Goats = 36 ÷ 12 = 3

⇒ Rows for Sheep = 60 ÷ 12 = 5

⇒ Total Rows = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 rows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder. Used to find the largest size of containers or groups.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest multiple that is exactly divisible by every number in a set. Used for recurring events like bells tolling or runners meeting.

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers a and b: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01aef6aa22c065b1ff3328b4dead48d2fd7d12beaf041f3f9bd0273d6d9dca25.png]

questions.question: If the price of a Pen is reduced by 30 Percent, it enables the customer to buy 5 more pens for Rs. 140. Find the reduced rate of Pen.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Amount saved due to **30% reduction** = 30% of Rs. 140

⇒ Savings = 0.30 × 140 = **Rs. 42**

This saved amount of **Rs. 42** allows the **customer** to buy **5 more pens**.

⇒ Reduced rate of **Pen** = Total savings ÷ Extra quantity = 42 ÷ 5 = **Rs. 8.4**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total expenditure = **Rs. 140**, Price reduction = **30%**, Extra quantity = **5 pens**.

**Formula Used:** Price × Consumption = Expenditure (If expenditure is constant, Price ∝ 1 / Consumption)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78346747b0e73b8b81d388c9e84afb47f61958e3130ff2112dab492e2abf4f88.png] 

⇒ Let original price be 100 units. After **30% reduction**, new price = 70 units.

⇒ Price Ratio (Old : New) = 100 : 70 = **10 : 7**

⇒ Since expenditure is constant (Rs. 140), Consumption Ratio (Old : New) = **7 : 10**

⇒ Increase in consumption = 10 − 7 = 3 units

⇒ According to question: 3 units = 5 pens

⇒ New consumption (10 units) = (5 ÷ 3) × 10 = **50/3 pens**

⇒ Reduced rate = Total expenditure ÷ New consumption

⇒ Reduced rate = 140 ÷ (50/3) = (140 × 3) ÷ 50

⇒ Reduced rate = 420 ÷ 50 = **Rs. 8.4**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price-Consumption Relation

When the expenditure remains constant, the percentage increase in consumption due to a reduction in price is given by: [x / (100 − x)] × 100, where x is the reduction percentage.

Direct Formula for Reduced Price

Reduced Price = (Total Amount × Reduction %) ÷ Extra Quantity. Similarly, Original Price = Reduced Price × 100 ÷ (100 − Reduction %).

Percentage and Ratio Conversion

A reduction of 30% means the new value is 7/10 of the original value. The consumption must increase in the ratio of 10/7 to keep the product constant.</p

questions.question: Kanika took a loan of Rs. 10,000 for 2 years on compound interest at the rate of 5% per annum, interest being compounded annually. How much money would she have saved if she had taken the loan on simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The money saved is the difference between **Compound Interest (CI)** and **Simple Interest (SI)** for 2 years.

Formula for 2-year difference: **Difference = P × (R/100)²**

Given: **P = ₹10,000** and **R = 5%**.

Difference = 10,000 × (5 / 100)² = 10,000 × (25 / 10,000).

Difference = ₹25.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹10,000; Rate (R) = 5% p.a.; Time (T) = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed65ec9fee5ad391606c0c7a1022ca65f3ef3a9baa3e9ec5a5ae1456dded03af.png] 

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = (10,000 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹1,000.

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** for 1st year = 5% of 10,000 = ₹500.

⇒ Interest for 2ⁿd year = 5% of (Principal + Interest of 1st year) = 5% of 10,500.

⇒ CI for 2ⁿd year = ₹525.

⇒ Total CI for 2 years = 500 + 525 = ₹1,025.

⇒ Amount saved = **CI − SI** = 1,025 − 1,000 = ₹25.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is calculated as: Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years at rate R%, the effective CI rate is R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100. For 5%, it is 5 + 5 + 0.25 = 10.25%.

Compound Interest Compounded Half-Yearly

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2n) in the CI formula.

Speed = 108 km/h

Time = 3 h

**Formula:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

The distance covered by the car is 108 × 3 = 324 km.

If the speed is reduced by 27 km/h, the new speed is 108 - 27 = 81 km/h.

The new time taken by the car to cover the same distance is 324/81 = 4 h.

Therefore, the time taken by the car to cover the same distance will be 4 h.

**The answer is 4 h.**

questions.question: A college student spends 75% of his pocket money. When the pocket money increased by 20%, the expenditure also increased by 15%. What is the increase in the savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** = 75 : 25 = 3 : 1.

Using the weighted average method: **Income Increase** = (Exp × Exp% + Sav × Sav%) ÷ Total Ratio.

20% = (3 × 15% + 1 × x%) ÷ 4.

80 = 45 + x ⇒ x = 35%.

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Pocket Money** (Income) = 100 units

Initial **Expenditure** = 75% of 100 = 75 units

Initial **Savings** = 100 − 75 = 25 units

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/827ddea52434b1e942f8faf138dbad8e6219927a8facb4922167fc8162a1d9cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ New **Pocket Money** = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120 units

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 75 + 15% of 75 = 75 + 11.25 = 86.25 units

⇒ New **Savings** = New Income − New Expenditure = 120 − 86.25 = 33.75 units

⇒ Increase in **Savings** = 33.75 − 25 = 8.75 units

⇒ Percentage Increase in **Savings** = (8.75 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 0.35 × 100 = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The basic equation is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any change in two variables directly impacts the third.

Weighted Average (Alligation Method)

Percentage change in **Income** is the weighted average of percentage changes in **Expenditure** and **Savings**: %ΔI = (E × %ΔE + S × %ΔS) ÷ (E + S).

Percentage Change Formula

To find the percentage increase or decrease, use: **[(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100**.</p

questions.question: A boat man goes 6 km against the current of the stream in 2 hours and goes 1.5 km along the current in 7.5 minutes. How long will (in hours) it take to go 30 km in still water?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance against the current = 6 km, Time taken = 2 hours.

Distance along the current = 1.5 km, Time taken = 7.5 minutes = 7.5/60 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed in still water = (Speed downstream + Speed upstream) / 2

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed upstream = 6 / 2 = 3 km/hr.

Speed downstream = 1.5 / (7.5/60) = 1.5 / (1/8) = 12 km/hr.

Speed in still water = (3 + 12) / 2 = 15 / 2 = 7.5 km/hr.

To go 30 km in still water, time taken = 30 / 7.5 = 4 hours.

**It will take 4 hours to go 30 km in still water.**

questions.question: If 3 tan θ = 2, find the value of (2 sintheta-costheta)/(2 costheta-sintheta).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **3 tan θ = 2**, we have **tan θ = 2/3**, which means **sin θ / cos θ = 2/3**.

For a **homogeneous expression** in sin θ and cos θ, we can directly substitute **sin θ = 2** and **cos θ = 3**.

Expression = (2 sin θ − cos θ) ÷ (2 cos θ − sin θ)

Substituting values: (2 × 2 − 3) ÷ (2 × 3 − 2) = (4 − 3) ÷ (6 − 2) = **1/4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 tan θ = 2 ⇒ **tan θ = 2/3**

**Formula Used:** tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dce9b1c8da4f27762fb740df37044bafb17a3638896ff3fcf8ab3d4bdde965c.png] 

⇒ Expression = (2 sin θ − cos θ) ÷ (2 cos θ − sin θ)

⇒ Divide the numerator and denominator by **cos θ**:

⇒ [(2 sin θ / cos θ) − (cos θ / cos θ)] ÷ [(2 cos θ / cos θ) − (sin θ / cos θ)]

⇒ (2 tan θ − 1) ÷ (2 − tan θ)

⇒ Now, substitute **tan θ = 2/3** into the simplified expression:

⇒ [2 × (2/3) − 1] ÷ [2 − (2/3)]

⇒ (4/3 − 1) ÷ (6/3 − 2/3)

⇒ (1/3) ÷ (4/3) = 1/4

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For any angle θ, **tan θ = sin θ / cos θ** and **cot θ = cos θ / sin θ = 1 / tan θ**.

Homogeneous Expressions

When every term in a fraction involves **sin θ** or **cos θ** to the same power, dividing by **cos θ** converts the entire expression into a function of **tan θ**.

Pythagorean Relation

In a right triangle, **sin θ = p/h**, **cos θ = b/h**, and **tan θ = p/b**. The relationship is defined by **h² = p² + b²**.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a book at 30% discount and still manages to earn 40% profit. In the next year, he give 10% discount on the book of same marked price and still manage to earn 50% profit. Find the per cent increase in the cost price of the book in the next year.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** is given by (100 − D%) : (100 + P%).

Year 1: CP₁ : MP = (100 − 30) : (100 + 40) = 70 : 140 = 1 : 2 = 5 : 10.

Year 2: CP₂ : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 50) = 90 : 150 = 3 : 5 = 6 : 10.

Since **MP** is same, **CP** increases from 5 to 6 units.

Percentage increase in CP = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First year: **Discount** = 30%, **Profit** = 40%

Next year: **Discount** = 10%, **Profit** = 50%, **Marked Price** is constant.

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5713e6cf42cd39430f7b9a9638b4cf5ecc74022305d8c2980add1cdfecccbf54.png] 

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** of the book be 100.

⇒ Year 1: SP₁ = 100 × (100 − 30) ÷ 100 = 70

⇒ Year 1: CP₁ = (70 × 100) ÷ (100 + 40) = 7000 ÷ 140 = 50

⇒ Year 2: SP₂ = 100 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100 = 90

⇒ Year 2: CP₂ = (90 × 100) ÷ (100 + 50) = 9000 ÷ 150 = 60

⇒ Increase in CP = CP₂ − CP₁ = 60 − 50 = 10

⇒ Percentage increase in CP = (10 ÷ 50) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

**__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is always CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This is the most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit.

Marked Price (MP)

MP is the price set by the seller, usually higher than CP. Discounts are always calculated on the MP, while Profit or Loss is always calculated on the CP.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.</p

questions.question: A pump can fill a tank with water in 3 hours. Because of a leak it took 3(1)/(5)hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water in the tank in
questions.solution:

Total Capacity = LCM of numerators of 3 and 16/5 = 48 units.

Combined Efficiency of Pump + Leak = 48 ÷ (16/5) = 15 units/hr.

Efficiency of Leak = 16 − 15 = 1 unit/hr (draining).

Time taken by Leak alone = Total Capacity ÷ Leak Efficiency = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 hours.

questions.question: Which key feature of Thomson’s Atomic Model helped explain the electrical neutrality of an atom?

options.text: The nucleus contained both, protons and neutrons
The positive charge was concentrated in the centre.
The positive and negative charges are equal in magnitude.
Electrons revolved around the nucleus in fixed orbits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The positive and negative charges are equal in magnitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thomson's atomic model**, also known as the "plum pudding model," proposed that an atom consists of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded in it.
 
• The model explained electrical neutrality by asserting that the **total positive and negative charges in an atom are equal in magnitude**, thereby balancing each other.
 
• Electrons, being negatively charged, were uniformly distributed throughout the positively charged "pudding," ensuring no net charge on the atom.
 
• This model laid the foundation for understanding the structure of atoms and their neutrality, despite its inability to explain atomic stability or spectral lines.
 
• The concept of equal positive and negative charges was a significant step toward uncovering the atomic structure, leading to further advancements in atomic theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: The nucleus contained both, protons and neutrons**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect in the context of Thomson's model because his model did not include the concept of a nucleus. The idea of a nucleus was introduced later by Rutherford.
 
• Protons and neutrons being located in the nucleus was established through Rutherford's and Chadwick's contributions, making this statement irrelevant to Thomson's theory.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: The positive charge was concentrated in the centre**
 
 
• This statement aligns with Rutherford's nuclear model, not Thomson's atomic model.
 
• In Rutherford's model, the atom was visualized as having a dense, positively charged nucleus at the center, surrounded by electrons. Thomson's model, in contrast, assumed a uniform distribution of positive charge.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Electrons revolved around the nucleus in fixed orbits**
 
 
• This concept is a feature of Bohr's atomic model, not Thomson's model.
 
• Bohr proposed that electrons travel in fixed orbits around the nucleus, explaining atomic stability and spectral lines, which Thomson's model could not address.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Thomson's Atomic Model**
 
 
• Thomson's atomic model was the first attempt to describe the internal structure of an atom.
 
• Though it was eventually replaced by more advanced models, it played a crucial role in shaping the early understanding of atomic structure.

questions.question: How many veto powers is vested in President of India?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The president has three veto powers, i.e. absolute, suspension & pocket.
 
• The president can send the bill back to parliament for changes, which constitutes a limited veto that can be overridden by a simple majority.
 
• But the Bill reconsidered by the parliament becomes law with or without the assents of the President after 14 days.
 
• The president can also take no action indefinitely on a bill, sometimes referred to as a pocket veto.
 
• The president can refuse to assent, which constitutes an absolute veto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

The three types of Vetoes are:

 
• Absolute Veto
 
• Suspensive Veto
 
• Pocket Veto

 
 

 **Absolute Veto**
 **Suspensive Veto**
 **Pocket Veto**
 
 

 The power of the President to withhold the assent to the bill is termed as his absolute veto
 The power of the President to return the bill to the Parliament with or without consideration is called the suspensive veto
 The power of the President to not act upon the bill is termed as a pocket veto
